scope.method: static analysis only; zero API, database, browser, or provider calls
scope.physicalCallDefinition: one client-side Atlas/OpenRouter fetch; provider-internal routing retries are outside the observable boundary
scope.configurationBasis: repository defaults, not a production-environment attestation

derivation.normalWrapperOuterAttempt: structured SDK operation (3) + prompt-JSON fallback SDK operation (3) + malformed-fallback JSON repair SDK operation (3)
derivation.forcedJsonWrapperOuterAttempt: prompt-JSON fallback SDK operation (3) + malformed-fallback JSON repair SDK operation (3)
derivation.ladderCallModel: parse failure on fireOnce #1, non-parse 400/reasoning failure on fireOnce #2, reasoning fallback fireOnce #3; each fireOnce has 3 SDK attempts
derivation.grammarPremiumLadder: three split cycles * (answer-only + add-decoys) + one repair in each cycle = 9 callLadderModel stages; 9 * 9

englishNonGrammar.meaning: one batched full-generation call plus at most one full-schema candidate-repair call per returned question

englishGrammarStrictOrRelaxedLegacy.meaning: one full-generation call, at most n full-schema candidate repairs, and at most n independent STANDARD grammar-solver calls

englishGrammarScarce.meaning: scarce mode omits the grammar solver but can still run candidate repair

eligiblePremiumGrammarStrict.meaning: ladder can exhaust and give up, then legacy generation, candidate repair, and grammar solver all run

koStrictNeedsSolver.meaning: KO skips candidate repair; strict mode can run one solver per returned question

symbols.H: AI SDK physical attempts per generateObject/generateText; current locked SDK default 3
symbols.n: requested questions in one plan item

runBounds.standardNonGrammarSingleType: (A + 2) * G * (1 + n): A strict passes, one relaxed pass, and at most one universal scarce/salvage pass
runBounds.standardGrammarSingleType: (A + 1) * G * (1 + 2n) + 2 * G * (1 + n): A strict passes, one rescue-or-relaxed solver pass, then at most grammar-scarce and universal-salvage passes
runBounds.premiumNonGrammarSingleType: (A + 1) * G * (1 + n): A strict passes plus at most one universal salvage pass
runBounds.premiumGrammarLadderSingleType: A * (L + 3G) + 2 * G * (1 + n), only when n=1 and all ladder eligibility predicates hold
runBounds.multiTypePlan: attempt class is selected by the strongest trigger anywhere in the plan; every strict/relaxed/salvage pass maps all plan items concurrently, so the physical cap is the sum of per-item pass caps, not the maximum
runBounds.autoPlanner: the legacy auto route adds one more G for planning before the engine

primaryFastPathDefaultConfigPerItem.premiumMaxCase: eligible triple ladder exhausts before legacy generation/repair/solver; A=2

reasons: GEMINI_QUESTION_MAX_RETRIES and GEMINI_QUESTION_EMPTY_RESULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS accept any positive integer and have no hard maximum.
The legacy direct single route normalizes count with no server-side upper bound; the legacy auto planner schema bounds neither plan length nor per-item count.
The primary UI emits one fast request per configured item and the server has no aggregate batch/campaign physical-call cap.
The production no-research-scope provider transport is an exact native-fetch passthrough and performs no lease or cap check.
Deadlines are time stops, not physical-call stops; immediately failing requests can consume many calls before a deadline.
A Trigger process crash after provider calls but before terminal job persistence can replay a run; normal caught failures mark FAILED and later task attempts skip, but the crash window remains.

observabilityGaps: usageEvents and result.attempts are logical-operation telemetry, not physical-call telemetry.
AI SDK retry failures are not aggregated into the successful result usage.
prompt-JSON fallback returns only the first generateText result usage; the JSON repair continuation usage is discarded.
failed ladder fireOnce calls emit undefined usage, and successful fireOnce usage does not expose preceding SDK retry usage.
therefore current cost records cannot prove a physical-call or USD cap.
requiredBudgetControllerInvariants: Reject execution unless endpoint, model, plan, schema, parser, prompt, retry policy, and price snapshot match a frozen allowlist.
Atomically reserve one physical-call slot and a conservative token/USD lease immediately before every provider fetch, including SDK retries.
Attribute every physical call to operation, candidate, type, plan, quality mode, stage, logical attempt, and monotonically increasing physical ordinal.
Count failed, timed-out, aborted, parse-invalid, and unknown-usage calls; unknown billing must settle to the reserved worst case, never zero.
Give JSON repair, prompt-JSON fallback, grammar answer-only, add-decoys, ladder repair, legacy candidate repair, and solver calls explicit child scopes.
Persist reservations and settlements durably so process crashes and Trigger retries share one job/campaign envelope.
Require all three caps before launch: candidate cap, physical-call cap, and USD cap; a deadline is only an additional stop condition.
Validate bounded request count, plan length, unique type entries, retry environment values, and max-output-token values before any call.
Reserve the full remaining worst-case envelope before starting an assignment, or stop before the assignment; never truncate a production policy mid-assignment and label it parity.
Use atomic campaign-wide accounting under Promise.all and client fast-request concurrency.
Fail closed on missing research scope/controller, ledger write failure, price ambiguity, endpoint/model drift, or incomplete response-clone settlement.
Reconcile final ledger physical ordinals against boundary observations and reject the entire phase on gaps or duplicates.
